title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This page is from the continuation of 'La Longue Marche' (§IV, 'les trois cas particuliers fondamentaux'). The objects are:
- the profinite group π̂_{0,3} of P^1 − {0,1,∞};
- its symmetric extension π̂_{0,3}^~, which adds the involutions σ_∞ (z ↦ 1−z, fixing ∞ and swapping 0 and 1), ρ (order 3) and τ_∞;
- a big group M^{!~}_{0,3}, an extension of a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group N^{!}_{0,3} by π̂_{0,3}. Its elements u are described by four equivalent parameter systems (g,h,f), (α_0,β_0,f), (α,β,f), (ξ,η,f).

The page continues the 1st special case from the previous page: h = 1, equivalently β = f, equivalently [u,σ_∞] = 1. In this case the data reduce to pairs (α,β) in π̂_{0,3} satisfying the loop equation (37)=(97):
  α ρ(α)^{-1} = β σ_∞(β)^{-1} · l^ν,
then completed to a triple by putting f = β. After renormalising α_0 = l^ν α (the conventions of §4), this reads ξ = l^ν η, with ξ = α_0 ρ(α_0)^{-1} and η = f σ_∞(f)^{-1}. A cancelled line started the '2nd case' (ξ = 1, i.e. f = α) prematurely; Grothendieck moved it to the next page.

The key observation, using (79), is formula (98). The image of u in GL(2,Ẑ) (the linear action on the abelianised fundamental group of the associated elliptic/double-cover situation) has the form
  μ (t σ_∞ + u') τ_∞^{α_2}.
Here σ_∞ acts as a matrix with σ_∞^2 = −1, so Ẑ[σ_∞] ≅ Ẑ[i]. By (99), τ_∞ σ_∞ τ_∞^{-1} = −σ_∞. Hence the image normalises the subalgebra Ẑ[σ_∞] ⊂ M_2(Ẑ); on the next page this is the normaliser of the non-split torus {tσ_∞ + u : t^2 + u^2 ∈ Ẑ^*}.

Grothendieck then defines (100) the centraliser subgroup M^{!~}_{0,3}(1/2) = {u : [u,σ_∞] = 1}. It is the stabiliser attached to the σ_∞-fixed point λ = 1/2, and it maps isomorphically onto N^{!}_{0,3}. This gives a canonical section, a splitting of the extension over the 'point 1/2'. The page ends announcing that the composite N → M(1/2) → GL(2,Ẑ) factors through the normaliser of the Cartan torus.

Modern reading: the 'tangential base point' at the special point λ = 1/2, whose S_3-orbit {−1, 2, 1/2} is the Legendre λ-orbit of the CM curve with j = 1728, yields a GT-type section. Its image in GL_2(Ẑ) lies in the normaliser of the Cartan subgroup Ẑ[i]^*. This is a combinatorial-anabelian analogue of Deuring/Serre's description of Galois images of CM elliptic curves.
errors: The letter u is used both for the group element u ∈ M^{!~}_{0,3} and for a scalar entry in (98) 't σ_∞ + u': a notational clash, not a mathematical error.
The cancelled '2° cas' line was started prematurely and then moved to the next page.

On the next page's margin, the orbit {1/2, 2, −1} is attributed to j = 0. Under the Legendre λ-parametrisation this orbit corresponds to j = 1728, which is consistent with the Ẑ[i]-torus found here. j = 0 corresponds to λ = e^{±iπ/3}, the ρ-fixed case treated next. Possibly a slip, or a different normalisation of the λ ↔ j correspondence.
(97) is written with an unexplained factor l^ν (written b^ν in the transcription); its precise meaning depends on (37) and the conventions of §4, which are not on this page.

ideas.what: Restricting the loop (hexagon-type) equation to elements commuting with the involution σ_∞; this gives a section of the extension over N^{!}_{0,3} attached to the fixed point 1/2.
ideas.modern_name: Torsion/fixed-point elements and splittings of GT-hat; tangential base points at special points of M_{0,4}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura, later Hoshi–Minamide–Mochizuki (profinite braid group automorphisms)

ideas.what: The image in GL(2,Ẑ) of the σ_∞-centralising subgroup lies in the normaliser of the non-split Cartan torus Ẑ[σ_∞] ≅ Ẑ[i], with τ_∞ acting as complex conjugation.
ideas.modern_name: Normaliser of Cartan subgroup (CM image, j = 1728), à la Serre/Deuring
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deuring, Serre (for Galois images of CM elliptic curves)

ideas.what: Changing α by l^ν to normalise the parameters (α_0 = l^ν α).

missed.claim: The GT-type subgroup fixing the special point 1/2 (equivalently, commuting with the order-2 symmetry σ_∞) maps to GL_2(Ẑ) through the normaliser of the Cartan torus Ẑ[i]^*. This is a purely combinatorial/anabelian counterpart of the CM structure of the j = 1728 curve. On the next page Grothendieck conjectures this is the only such factorisation, then retracts in the margin ('Si seulement cela était!').
missed.quote: et impliquent que u = u_{α,β,f} normalise la sous-algèbre de l'algèbre des matrices M_2(Ẑ) engendrée par σ_∞
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It links GT-hat elements with prescribed fixed points to CM Galois images (normalisers of Cartan subgroups). This is relevant to studies of 'eigenloci' and special points in GT theory and to explicit GT actions on π_1 of M_{1,1}. As far as I know, the literature does not state it in this form.

deep.surprise_reason: A coherent unpublished detail: special-point sections of a GT-type extension landing in normalisers of Cartan tori. The ingredients (GT symmetries, CM images) are known, but this explicit link and its j-invariant classification are not clearly in print. It is not a major new result.
transcription_corrections: 'b^ν' is likely 'l_1^ν' (or l^ν), as on the previous page (96).
'c'était les commutations dans f_4 h' should probably read 'c'étaient les conventions du §4' (followed by '(où la formule prend alors la forme').
'(que l'on complètera dans un premier f=β)' probably reads '(qu'on complètera en un triple en prenant f = β)'.
In the underbrace the label reads 'η' (f σ_∞(f)^{-1} = η), not 'φ=η'.
The marginal note likely reads '(α,β) ↦ (l^{-ν}α, l^{-ν}β) automorphismes ...'.
